en: Points of Controversy:
The Chapter on Latent Dispositions,
Thirteenth Section.
The Discussion on the Worldling:
Does a worldling remain for an eon?
Yes, he does.
Is it the case that a world-cycle is established and a Buddha appears in the world?
One should not say so… [as before]… Could one who has the lifespan of a world-cycle remain for a world-cycle?
“Yes,” [you say].
“The world-age is forming and the Saṅgha is splitting?
You should not speak thus …pe…
“Does one who stands for an eon remain for an eon?”—
“Yes.
“And does the eon collapse while one who stands for an eon performs karma that endures for an eon?”— “No.”
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Would an aeon-endurer remain for an aeon? Yes.
Is it the case that the aeon is established and yet a person who has reached the end of an aeon dies?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Would a person who has reached the end of an aeon remain for the duration of an aeon?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then could it remain for a past aeon? Could it remain for a future aeon?
You should not say so …pe…
"Could one who has attained the status of an endurer of an eon remain for an eon?
"Yes.
"Could he remain for two eons... could he remain for three eons... could he remain for four eons?"
It should not be said so … [as before] … Would an aeon-dweller remain for an aeon? Yes.
"When the aeon is burning up, where does one who has reached the end of his aeon go?
"He goes to another world-system.
"Does he go having died, or does he go through the air?"
"The dead man goes.
Is karma that lasts for an eon (*kappaṭṭhiya*) maturing in a subsequent life (*aparāpariyavepakka*)?
One should not say so... [and so forth].
“He goes through the air,” you say?
“Yes. “Is he one who has attained the status of an aeon and possesses psychic power? “Yes.”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses supernormal power (iddhimā) a world-endurer (kappaṭṭha)? Yes.

Is it to be said that, in the sense of "lasting for an eon" (*kappaṭṭha*), the basis of psychic power consisting of zeal is developed, the basis of psychic power consisting of energy is developed, the basis of psychic power consisting of consciousness is developed, and the basis of psychic power consisting of investigation is developed?
One should not say so... [etc.
...One should not say so.
“Would one who has reached the end of an aeon remain for an aeon?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Subject to states of deprivation, destined for hell,
staying there for an eon is the schism-maker of the Saṅgha;
delighting in factions, established in what is not Dhamma.”
Falls away from the security of yoga;
having split a harmonious Saṅgha,
one roasts in hell for an eon.
Is that indeed a sutta? Yes.
In that case, one who has reached the end of an aeon would remain for an aeon.
The commentary on the kappaṭṭha is finished.
